editorNote: A light weekend for the watchlist: a broad AI-led rally gave stocks their first winning week in three, Alphabet is testing its long-shot bet on computing from orbit, and bitcoin ETFs just posted their best week of the year. Nothing here is a single-name earnings or regulatory event — the moves are macro and infrastructure, not headlines about one ticker.

stories.headline: Wall Street posts its first winning week in three as AI stocks lead a rebound
stories.summary: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72, each up 0.5% on the day and 1.2% and 2.1% for the week, as gains in AI and chip stocks and a pullback in oil below $98/barrel offset a Treasury-yield spike to 5.20% — its highest since 2007 — earlier in the week.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the market's first weekly gain in three, showing AI-linked names still have room to rally even as elevated bond yields keep pressuring the broader tape.

sourceLinks.title: U.S. Stocks End Higher After Volatile Week – Sept. 26

stories.headline: Alphabet moves up its first orbital AI-satellite launch to October 1
stories.summary: Google says a prototype satellite carrying its TPU chips will launch October 1 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rideshare mission for Project Suncatcher, gathering in-orbit data on how the chips handle launch vibration, radiation and thermal extremes; a second milestone pairing two satellites to test laser interconnects is planned for 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: It's Alphabet's first hardware test of computing from orbit, an early and speculative extension of its AI infrastructure spending that a Google VP says won't be "usefully operational" for years.

stories.headline: US bitcoin ETFs pull in $2.4 billion in their best week of 2026
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in a combined $2.4 billion between September 21 and 25 — led by a $999 million single-day haul on the 21st that tapered to $134 million by Friday — their strongest week of the year, after entering the week roughly $1 billion in the red for 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: The week's inflows pushed 2026 year-to-date bitcoin ETF flows back into positive territory, though the sharp daily decline through the week suggests the momentum may already be cooling.

sourceLinks.title: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Reach $2.4 Billion This Week, But Daily Figures Decline
